title: Menew: free Mac menu bar app with system monitor & clipboard manager
meta_desc: Menew is a free, open source menu bar app for macOS: system monitor, clipboard history with search (⌘⇧V), quick actions, keyboard cleaning mode and more.
og_desc: System monitor, clipboard history, quick actions and cleaning mode. Free and open source.
lead: System monitor, clipboard history with instant search, one-click quick actions and a cleaning mode — in one tiny, native app. No subscription. No account. No telemetry.
alt_panel: Clipboard history panel with search, filters and preview
alt_system: System monitor with CPU, memory, disk and battery rings
features_h2:
The little things you do every day,
one click away.
features_sub: Menew replaces a handful of paid menu bar utilities with one fast, native app built in Swift. With the Liquid Glass look of macOS 26. Use only what you need: turn modules off in Settings.
f1_d: CPU and GPU with live graphs, memory pressure and swap, disk space and read/write speed, battery health and cycles, and the busiest processes, which you can quit in one click. Optional alerts, and you choose what shows in the menu bar. Turn on your next meeting at the top of the menu, with a Join button for Zoom, Meet or Teams.
f2_d: Text, links, images and files. Instant search, filters, pins and a rich preview. Opens with ⌘⇧V. Pause it for 15 minutes or an hour when you copy something private. Turn on the paste queue to copy several things and paste them one by one with ⌘V, in order.
f3_d: Brightness for every screen, external monitors included. Mute the mic or the sound, hide the Dock, dark mode, keep awake with a timer, hidden files and desktop icons. Plus color picker, screenshot to clipboard, eject disks and more. Keep Awake also works until a set time or while an app is open.
f4_d: Clear caches, logs and developer junk in seconds. A deep scan finds old downloads, large files and duplicate files for you to review. Removed files go to the Trash.
f5_d: Live download and upload, local and public IP, and a real speed test powered by macOS itself. See which apps are using the network right now.
f6_d: Notes with #tags and Markdown checklists, protected notes that open with Touch ID, and reusable snippets in ⌘⇧V. Give a snippet an abbreviation like “;sig” and typing it anywhere turns it into the text.
clip_sub: Press ⌘⇧V anywhere, type a few letters and hit return. It pastes straight into the app you were using.
clip_l1: Smart previews — color swatches for hex codes, link previews, images and file icons.
clip_l2: Filters & pins — jump between text, links, images and files; keep favorites on top.
clip_l3: Password-safe — ignores anything marked as a password by 1Password, Keychain and friends. You can also pick apps to ignore, right from a list.
act_h2: Toggles you'd otherwise Google every time.
act_sub: Show hidden files, hide the desktop, keep the Mac awake for an hour or pick a color from anywhere on screen — without opening Terminal. Every switch shows its current state.
act_l1: Monitor brightness — a slider for every screen, including third-party monitors over DDC/CI. Monitors behind an adapter that blocks DDC are dimmed by software instead.
act_l2: Mute your mic — from any app with ⌃⌥⌘M, great for meetings.
act_l3: Window manager — snap windows to halves, corners and thirds with ⌃⌥ shortcuts or a grid, and send them to the other display.
act_l4: Command palette — press ⌃⌥Space to find any app, action, window layout, snippet or note. Type “brightness 60” or “awake 2h”. Do math and conversions too: “20% of 340”, “5 km to mi”. And it transforms the text you copied: UPPERCASE, camelCase, format JSON, Base64, count words.
act_l5: Work profiles — save your open apps and window layout, then bring it all back with one click: apps open, windows go back in place, mic and Keep Awake set.
act_l6: Quick shelf — shake files while dragging and a shelf appears. Drop files, links and text there, then drag them all out together. Originals never move.
act_l7: Automations — at 9 AM turn on your work profile, mute the mic when Zoom opens, dim the screen when you unplug, quit everything when a focus session starts, run one of your Shortcuts a minute before a meeting or when the Mac wakes. Simple triggers, no scripts.
act_l8: Copy text from screen — press ⌃⌥⌘T, select any area (a video, a PDF, an error message) and its text goes to the clipboard. Works on copied images too. Runs entirely on your Mac.
act_l9: Focus timer — start 25 minutes (or any time: type “focus 50” in the palette) and the countdown shows in the menu bar. It can mute the mic, keep the Mac awake and pause the clipboard, then puts it all back and gives you a 5-minute break.
act_l10: App control — quit all apps, quit everything but the one you're using, hide the rest or force quit a frozen app. A work profile can close everything else and open only what you need, and an automation can quit all apps when the battery hits 5%.
priv_h2: Your data never leaves your Mac.
priv_sub: Menew is open source, so you don't have to take our word for it.
priv1_d: The app sends nothing about you: no analytics, no tracking, no account. Ever.
priv2_d: History and notes live in ~/Library/Application Support/Menew.
priv3_d: Read it, fork it, improve it. Pull requests welcome.
final_h2: Make your menu bar work for you.
final_sub: Free forever. Takes ten seconds to install.
step3: Open Menew. It lives in your menu bar; press ⌘⇧V for the clipboard.
hint_dmg: macOS 14 or later · Apple Silicon & Intel · Signed and notarized by Apple
hint_brew: Newer Homebrew versions ask you to trust third-party taps once.
hint_src: Needs Xcode 16 or the Swift 6 toolchain.
ai_text: Using an AI assistant? Copy a ready-made prompt and paste it into ChatGPT, Claude or your terminal agent.
coffee_text: Menew is made in spare time. If it saves you a few minutes a day:
ai_prompt:
Install Menew on my Mac. It's a free, open source menu bar app (https://github.com/Quost/menew), signed and notarized by Apple, and it needs macOS 14 or later.

1. If Homebrew is installed, run:
   brew tap quost/menew https://github.com/Quost/menew
   brew trust quost/menew
   brew install --cask menew
2. Otherwise, download the latest Menew.dmg from https://github.com/Quost/menew/releases/latest, open it and copy Menew.app into /Applications.
3. Open Menew. It shows up in the menu bar; ⌘⇧V opens the clipboard history.

Explain each command before running it.
